findings.issue_text: Inverted condition in UsernamePasswordForm.challenge() causes error challenges for unidentified users (user == null) to lose WebAuthn/passkeys form data — the unknown/missing-username first-login path that previously called fillContextForm now silently does not, so the passkey/conditional-UI option vanishes from the error page after a failed first-login attempt in passkeys-enabled realms

UsernameForm calls a no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() that is not defined anywhere in this diff — if no such overload exists in unchanged code this is a build-breaking compile error; if it does exist, it must be verified it evaluates to true for UsernameForm's WebAuthn wiring or the intended re-auth passkey behavior is a silent no-op

USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH constant widened from protected to public in AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator, turning an internal auth-session note name into a permanent public API commitment for a widely subclassed extension point; hosting the constant in AuthenticatorUtils would achieve the same without expanding the base-class contract

Re-authentication skip in UsernameForm is gated on realm-level passkeys being enabled rather than anything user-specific, so password-only users re-authenticating with prompt=login now get an extra username page and the identity asserted during re-auth is no longer pinned (users can submit a different username)

New code path in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse (call to AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError) has zero test coverage - no test exercises a failed/cancelled passkey authentication during re-authentication to verify the re-auth layout (username hidden, registration disabled) is preserved

Condition inversion in UsernamePasswordForm.challenge(context, error, field) from 'context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth != null && isPasskeysEnabled()' to 'isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())' means the error page after a failed login with an unidentified user no longer gets WebAuthn conditional-UI setup via fillContextForm - a likely unintended regression with no test asserting either the old or new behavior

Negative assertion in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey uses catch (Exception) which swallows arbitrary WebDriver failures (timeout, stale session, page not loaded) as 'element absent', creating a false-pass risk; fail(...) is unreachable dead code since findElement throws rather than returning null, and the stricter Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) used pre-PR should be restored

No test coverage of UsernameForm-based re-authentication for a password-only user while passkeys are enabled - the path 'passkeys enabled → prompt=login → manually submit username → password re-auth', including the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH note interplay controlling username hiding, is untested and could break the handoff to password re-authentication for non-passkey users

goldens.comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inverted condition in UsernamePasswordForm.challenge() causes error challenges for unidentified users (user == null) to lose WebAuthn/passkeys form data — the unknown/missing-username first-login path that previously called fillContextForm now silently does not, so the passkey/conditional-UI option vanishes from the error page after a failed first-login attempt in passkeys-enabled realms

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `UsernamePasswordForm.challenge(context, error, field)` from calling `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` when `context.getUser() == null` (and passkeys enabled) to calling it only when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true. But `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` explicitly requires `user != null`, so the error-challenge path for unidentified users will no longer populate WebAuthn/passkeys form context. This directly matches the finding’s claim that, after a failed attempt where the user is still null (e.g., missing/unknown username), the subsequent error page can lose passkeys/conditional-UI setup that previously would have been retained via `fillContextForm`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly widens `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` in `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` from `protected static final` to `public static final` (first hunk). It is then referenced from `AuthenticatorUtils` via a static import (`import static ...AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH;`). This does expand the public surface/contract of a widely used base authenticator class just to share an auth-session note key with a utility method, which is an architectural/API-scope concern rather than a functional defect. The finding’s suggested alternative (hosting the constant elsewhere to avoid expanding the base-class contract) is consistent with what the diff shows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Re-authentication skip in UsernameForm is gated on realm-level passkeys being enabled rather than anything user-specific, so password-only users re-authenticating with prompt=login now get an extra username page and the identity asserted during re-auth is no longer pinned (users can submit a different username)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes UsernameForm.authenticate() from skipping the username form whenever context.getUser() != null (re-authentication case) to skipping only when context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() (services/.../UsernameForm.java). This means that when conditional passkeys are enabled, the username step will no longer be skipped even though the user is already identified, causing an extra username page during re-authentication. Because the username form is an identity-selection step, showing it when a user is already set can allow switching the asserted identity unless other (not shown) logic prevents it; nothing in this diff adds such pinning for UsernameForm.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new call in `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse()` to `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)`, which changes UI attributes on passkey error during re-authentication. The accompanying tests added/modified in this diff cover successful passkey re-authentication and password failures during re-authentication, but none exercise a *failed/cancelled conditional passkey attempt during re-authentication* that would drive the `createErrorResponse()` path and assert that `USERNAME_HIDDEN` / `REGISTRATION_DISABLED` are preserved. The claim of "zero test coverage" repo-wide can’t be proven from the diff alone, but the new path is not covered by tests shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Negative assertion in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey uses catch (Exception) which swallows arbitrary WebDriver failures (timeout, stale session, page not loaded) as 'element absent', creating a false-pass risk; fail(...) is unreachable dead code since findElement throws rather than returning null, and the stricter Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) used pre-PR should be restored

adjudication.rationale: In PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey(), the absence check is implemented as `try { driver.findElement(...); ... } catch (Exception nsee) { // expected }`. The diff shows it catches any `Exception`, so unrelated WebDriver/runtime failures (e.g., stale session, timing issues) could be misinterpreted as “element absent”, creating false-pass risk. Also, `fail("Not expected to have webauthn button")` is effectively dead/unreachable because `findElement(...)` returns a non-null WebElement or throws; the preceding `assertThat(..., nullValue())` can never succeed. A more precise `assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` (or checking `findElements().isEmpty()`) would avoid swallowing arbitrary failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test coverage of UsernameForm-based re-authentication for a password-only user while passkeys are enabled - the path 'passkeys enabled → prompt=login → manually submit username → password re-auth', including the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH note interplay controlling username hiding, is untested and could break the handoff to password re-authentication for non-passkey users

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds/changes re-authentication behavior around conditional passkeys and the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH note (constant made public; new AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError used in AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler and WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator). It also changes UsernameForm.authenticate to *not* skip the username form during re-auth when conditional passkeys are enabled (`if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())`). The added/updated tests cover re-authentication for passkey users (discoverable/external key) and a password-only re-auth scenario only when realm passkeys are disabled (`setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)` in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey), but there is no test in the diff covering the specific username-first (UsernameForm) re-auth path for a password-only user with realm passkeys enabled, including the username-submit → password step and the username-hiding behavior controlled by USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH on error. That’s a concrete, diff-grounded test gap, not a proven functional bug from the diff alone.
